title: 2 Kings Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 10.

questions.question: How many sons did Ahab have in Samaria?
options: Seventy
Fifty
Thirty
One hundred
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:1 states that Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria.

questions.question: To whom did Jehu send letters from Samaria?
options: The rulers of Jezreel, the elders, and those who raised Ahab's children
The priests of Baal
The people of Jerusalem
The prophets of Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: The rulers of Jezreel, the elders, and those who raised Ahab's children
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:1 says Jehu wrote letters and sent them to the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders, and to those who brought up Ahab's children.

questions.question: What did Jehu command them to do with the best of Ahab's sons?
options: Set him on his father's throne and fight for his house
Send him to Egypt
Hide him in a secret place
Make him priest of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Set him on his father's throne and fight for his house
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:3 instructs to look out the best and meetest of Ahab's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for his house.

questions.question: How did the rulers and elders respond to Jehu's first letter?
options: They were exceedingly afraid and doubted their ability to stand against Jehu
They immediately obeyed and crowned a son
They sent gifts to Jehu
They ignored the letter
questions.correctAnswer: They were exceedingly afraid and doubted their ability to stand against Jehu
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:4 states that they were exceedingly afraid, noting two kings had not stood against Jehu, so they doubted they could.

questions.question: What did the rulers and those who raised Ahab's children declare to Jehu in their message?
options: They were his servants and would do all he commanded
They declared war against Jehu
They wanted to crown a new king themselves
They asked for peace negotiations
questions.correctAnswer: They were his servants and would do all he commanded
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:5 says they sent word to Jehu declaring themselves his servants and that they would do all he bade them.

questions.question: What did Jehu instruct them to do in his second letter?
options: Take the heads of the king's sons and bring them to Jezreel
Prepare a feast for Baal
Crown the eldest son of Ahab
Hide the king's sons from him
questions.correctAnswer: Take the heads of the king's sons and bring them to Jezreel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:6 records Jehu's second letter commanding them to take the heads of Ahab's sons and bring them to Jezreel.

questions.question: What was done with the heads of Ahab's sons after they were killed?
options: They were put in baskets and sent to Jehu
They were buried secretly
They were burned on a pyre
They were thrown into the river
questions.correctAnswer: They were put in baskets and sent to Jehu
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:7 states that the heads were put in baskets and sent to Jehu at Jezreel.

questions.question: What did Jehu command to do with the heads when the messenger brought them to him?
options: Lay them in two heaps at the gate entrance until morning
Burn them immediately
Hide them from the people
Bury them in the field
questions.correctAnswer: Lay them in two heaps at the gate entrance until morning
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:8 shows Jehu ordering the heads to be laid in two heaps at the gate entrance until the morning.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu admitted to conspiring against and killing his master before the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:9 records Jehu standing before the people and confessing he conspired against and slew his master.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu claimed that the word of the LORD concerning the house of Ahab had failed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:10 declares that nothing of the LORD's word concerning Ahab's house had fallen to the earth; the LORD fulfilled His word.

questions.question: Who did Jehu kill in Jezreel after receiving the heads of Ahab's sons?
options: All remaining of Ahab's house, great men, kinsfolks, and priests
Only Ahab's servants
Only the priests of Baal
The people of Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: All remaining of Ahab's house, great men, kinsfolks, and priests
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:11 states Jehu slew all that remained of Ahab's house in Jezreel, including his great men, kinsfolks, and priests.

questions.question: Where did Jehu go after killing those in Jezreel?
options: To Samaria
To Jerusalem
To Dan
To Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: To Samaria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:12 says Jehu arose and departed to Samaria after the events in Jezreel.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu spared some of Ahaziah's brothers when he met them by the shearing house.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:14 states Jehu took Ahaziah's brothers alive but then slew all forty-two of them, leaving none alive.

questions.question: What was the first thing Jehu did when he arrived in Jezreel according to the chapter?
options: Ordered the heads of Ahab's sons to be laid at the gate
Sent a letter to the elders
Killed Ahaziah's brothers
Burned the house of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Ordered the heads of Ahab's sons to be laid at the gate
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:8 shows that upon receiving the heads, Jehu commanded them to be laid in two heaps at the gate entrance until morning, which is the first action recorded at Jezreel.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 10, which instruction comes first?
options: Look out the best of Ahab's sons and set him on the throne
Take the heads of Ahab's sons and bring them to Jezreel
Kill Ahaziah's brothers
Gather all the worshippers of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Look out the best of Ahab's sons and set him on the throne
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:3 records Jehu's first instruction to look out the best of Ahab's sons and set him on the throne before he sends a second letter to take their heads (2 Kings 10:6).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did Jehu meet on the way at the shearing house, and what did he ask him?
options: Jehonadab, son of Rechab, and he asked if his heart was right with Jehu's heart
The brethren of Ahaziah, and he asked who they were
The priests of Baal, and he asked them to worship the LORD
The elders of Jezreel, and he asked about Ahab's sons
questions.correctAnswer: Jehonadab, son of Rechab, and he asked if his heart was right with Jehu's heart
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 10:15, Jehu met Jehonadab the son of Rechab and asked him, 'Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart?' This shows Jehu's desire for alignment in zeal for the LORD, connecting also to verse 16 where Jehu invites Jehonadab to witness his zeal.

questions.question: What did Jehu instruct the men over the house of Baal to do after the burnt offering?
options: Go in and slay them; let none come forth
Join in worshipping the LORD
Release the worshippers of Baal
Build a new altar for Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Go in and slay them; let none come forth
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states that after the burnt offering, Jehu commanded the guard and captains to enter and kill all the worshippers of Baal, ensuring none escaped. This complements verse 24 where he appointed men to guard outside to prevent escape.

questions.question: How does Jehu's action toward the worshippers of Baal in 2 Kings 10:18-19 illustrate the virtue of zeal for God?
options: By boldly calling all Baal worshippers to a gathering to decisively remove their influence
By negotiating peace with the Baal priests
By quietly allowing Baal worship to continue
By building a temple for Baal worshippers
questions.correctAnswer: By boldly calling all Baal worshippers to a gathering to decisively remove their influence
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 show Jehu gathering the people and summoning the prophets and priests of Baal for a great sacrifice, intending to destroy Baal worshippers. This demonstrates his zeal for the LORD and obedience to God's commands.

questions.question: What promise does 2 Kings 10:30 give to Jehu because of his obedience in executing God's will?
options: His descendants would sit on the throne of Israel for four generations
He would become king of Judah
He would be wealthy and live long
He would build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: His descendants would sit on the throne of Israel for four generations
questions.explanation: Verse 30 states that because Jehu did what was right in the LORD's eyes, his children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne. This demonstrates God's reward for obedience and faithfulness.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 10:23 teach about the importance of discernment in spiritual matters?
options: Jehu and Jehonadab searched to ensure only Baal worshippers were present, excluding servants of the LORD
Jehu invited all to worship Baal to promote unity
Jehu ignored who was present in the house of Baal
Jehu allowed servants of the LORD to join Baal worship
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu and Jehonadab searched to ensure only Baal worshippers were present, excluding servants of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 23 records Jehu and Jehonadab instructing the worshippers to confirm that no servants of the LORD were among them, highlighting the importance of spiritual discernment to avoid compromising God's worship.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 10:14, Jehu spared some of the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah after capturing them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 14 clearly states that Jehu took the brethren of Ahaziah alive and then slew all forty-two men, leaving none remaining. This shows his thorough obedience in carrying out judgment.

questions.question: Why did Jehu call for vestments to be brought for the worshippers of Baal in 2 Kings 10:22?
options: To disguise himself and Jehonadab among them and execute judgment
To honor Baal with new garments
To clothe his own army
To prepare a feast for the people
questions.correctAnswer: To disguise himself and Jehonadab among them and execute judgment
questions.explanation: In verse 22, Jehu orders vestments for the Baal worshippers, which is part of his subtle plan (verse 19) to gather and then destroy them. This shows strategic obedience in executing God's will.

questions.question: What consequence did Jehu declare in 2 Kings 10:24 for anyone who lets a man escape from the hands of the Baal worshippers?
options: His life shall be for the life of him
He shall be rewarded
He shall be forgiven
He shall be made a priest
questions.correctAnswer: His life shall be for the life of him
questions.explanation: Verse 24 records Jehu appointing men to guard outside and warning that anyone who lets an enemy escape will lose his own life, emphasizing the seriousness of obedience and accountability.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 10:17 demonstrate the biblical virtue of obedience in leadership?
options: Jehu destroyed all remaining members of Ahab's house in Samaria, fulfilling the LORD's command
Jehu made peace with Ahab's descendants
Jehu spared many of Ahab's family
Jehu ignored the LORD's command
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu destroyed all remaining members of Ahab's house in Samaria, fulfilling the LORD's command
questions.explanation: Verse 17 shows Jehu's obedience by completely destroying Ahab's house in Samaria according to the word spoken by Elijah, illustrating faithful leadership in carrying out God's judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu fully followed the LORD's law with all his heart according to 2 Kings 10:31.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 31 explicitly says Jehu did not walk in the law of the LORD with all his heart and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, indicating incomplete obedience despite some faithfulness.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jehu's question to Jehonadab in 2 Kings 10:15, 'Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart'?
options: It emphasizes the importance of unity and shared zeal for the LORD
It is a greeting without deeper meaning
It questions Jehonadab's loyalty to Baal
It is a challenge to a contest
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the importance of unity and shared zeal for the LORD
questions.explanation: This question in verse 15 reflects Jehu's desire for partnership in wholehearted commitment to God's cause, linking to verse 16 where Jehu shows his zeal for the LORD.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 10:21 reveal about the gathering of Baal worshippers at Jehu's summons?
options: All Baal worshippers from Israel came, filling the house of Baal completely
Only a few Baal worshippers came
The Baal worshippers refused to come
Only priests came, not the people
questions.correctAnswer: All Baal worshippers from Israel came, filling the house of Baal completely
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that Jehu sent through all Israel and all the worshippers of Baal came, filling the house of Baal from end to end, showing complete participation for Jehu's plan.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Kings 10:28 states that Jehu completely destroyed Baal worship out of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 28 clearly says 'Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel,' confirming the complete removal of Baal worship under Jehu's leadership.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 10:13-14, what was the fate of the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah when Jehu met them?
options: They were taken alive and then slain at the pit of the shearing house
They were welcomed and spared
They escaped
They joined Jehu's army
questions.correctAnswer: They were taken alive and then slain at the pit of the shearing house
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 14 record Jehu questioning the brethren of Ahaziah, taking them alive, and then killing all forty-two men without leaving any alive, showing decisive judgment.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 10:19 teach about the use of subtlety in fulfilling God's purposes?
options: Jehu used subtlety to gather Baal worshippers for destruction, showing wisdom in obedience
Jehu openly confronted Baal worshippers without any plan
Jehu ignored God's commands
Jehu worshipped Baal to blend in
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu used subtlety to gather Baal worshippers for destruction, showing wisdom in obedience
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explains Jehu's subtle approach in calling all Baal worshippers to a sacrifice to ultimately destroy them, demonstrating strategic obedience to God's will.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 10.

questions.question: What did Jehu command his guards and captains to do after the burnt offering was completed in the house of Baal?
options: Let the worshippers go free
Slay them all; let none come forth
Bind the worshippers and imprison them
Celebrate with a feast
questions.correctAnswer: Slay them all; let none come forth
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:25 states that Jehu told the guards and captains to go in and slay all the worshippers so that none could escape.

questions.question: After killing the worshippers, what did Jehu's men do with the images from the house of Baal?
options: They hid them in caves
They sold them to foreign merchants
They brought them out and burned them
They placed them in the temple of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They brought them out and burned them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:26 says that after the slaughter, the images were brought out of the house of Baal and burned by Jehu's men.

questions.question: What was done to the house of Baal after Jehu destroyed the images?
options: It was converted into a temple for the LORD
It was made into a draught house
It was left intact as a warning
It was given to the priests of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: It was made into a draught house
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:27 shows that the house of Baal was broken down and made into a draught house, meaning a place to dry grain or chaff.

questions.question: Despite Jehu's destruction of Baal worship, which sin did he not depart from according to the chapter?
options: Worshipping the golden calves in Bethel and Dan
Idolatry with Asherah poles
Child sacrifice
Worshipping Molech
questions.correctAnswer: Worshipping the golden calves in Bethel and Dan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:29 clearly states Jehu did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, specifically the golden calves set up in Bethel and Dan.

questions.question: What promise did the LORD make to Jehu because of his actions against the house of Ahab?
options: Jehu would have a long life
His children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne
He would be king over all Israel and Judah
He would be remembered as a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: His children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:30 records the LORD's promise that Jehu's descendants to the fourth generation would sit on the throne of Israel for executing justice against Ahab's house.

questions.question: True or False: Jehu fully obeyed the LORD's law with all his heart during his reign.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:31 states that Jehu did not walk in the law of the LORD with all his heart, continuing in the sins of Jeroboam.

questions.question: Who began to afflict Israel during Jehu's reign, attacking all its borders?
options: Hazael
Sennacherib
Nebuchadnezzar
Pharaoh Necho
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:32 identifies Hazael as the one who smote Israel in all its coasts during Jehu's reign.

questions.question: Which regions east of the Jordan did Hazael conquer during Jehu's time?
options: Gilead, Gad, Reuben, Manasseh, Bashan
Moab and Ammon
Philistia and Edom
Zion and Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Gilead, Gad, Reuben, Manasseh, Bashan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:33 lists these eastern territories as those taken by Hazael during Jehu's reign.

questions.question: Where can the full record of Jehu's deeds and might be found according to the chapter?
options: In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
In the book of Psalms
In the book of the Law of Moses
In the scrolls found in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:34 informs us that Jehu's acts are written in the chronicles of Israel’s kings.

questions.question: How long did Jehu reign over Israel in Samaria?
options: 28 years
40 years
7 years
15 years
questions.correctAnswer: 28 years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:36 states Jehu reigned for twenty and eight years in Samaria.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Jehu and Jehonadab the son of Rechab as described in the chapter?
options: Jehu greeted him warmly and invited him to ride in his chariot
Jehu imprisoned Jehonadab for opposing Baal worship
Jehu ignored Jehonadab and his greetings
Jehu and Jehonadab fought over the kingship
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu greeted him warmly and invited him to ride in his chariot
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 10:15-16 describes Jehu meeting Jehonadab, greeting him, confirming their shared zeal for the LORD, and taking him into his chariot.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Jehu's destruction of Baal worship while continuing Jeroboam's sin with the golden calves?
options: Irony
Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: The contrast between Jehu’s zeal in destroying Baal worship and his failure to remove the golden calves is an example of irony, showing partial obedience (2 Kings 10:28-31).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage foretold the LORD’s judgment on Ahab’s house that Jehu fulfilled?
options: Exodus 20
Genesis 12:1-3
Psalm 23
questions.explanation: Jehu's actions fulfilled the prophecy Elijah gave in 1 Kings 21:19-24 concerning the judgment on Ahab’s house, as reiterated in 2 Kings 10:10.

questions.question: Which New Testament book references Jehu’s zeal in a positive light as an example of righteous anger?
options: Romans
Hebrews
James
Revelation
questions.correctAnswer: James
questions.explanation: James 4:6-7 discusses submitting to God and resisting the devil, often referencing Old Testament zeal as a model; Jehu’s zeal (2 Kings 10:16-17) can be seen as a typological example of righteous anger.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'zeal' used by Jehu when declaring his commitment to serve the LORD most closely means:
options: Passionate devotion
Casual interest
Fearful obedience
Indifference
questions.correctAnswer: Passionate devotion
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word קִנְאָה (qin'ah) used here (2 Kings 10:16) conveys passionate zeal or fervent devotion, emphasizing Jehu’s intense commitment to God’s cause.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was Jehu's initial strategy to eliminate Ahab's sons as described in 2 Kings 10:1-7?
options: He invited them to a feast and poisoned them.
He wrote letters to Samaria’s rulers to kill Ahab’s sons and send their heads to him.
He ambushed them on the battlefield.
He exiled them to a distant land.
questions.correctAnswer: He wrote letters to Samaria’s rulers to kill Ahab’s sons and send their heads to him.
questions.explanation: Jehu's strategy involved writing letters to Samaria's rulers commanding them to kill Ahab's sons and send their heads to him, as detailed in 2 Kings 10:1-7.

questions.question: What theological truth is demonstrated by Jehu’s statement in 2 Kings 10:10 about the word of the LORD?
options: God’s word is conditional and can be broken.
Nothing of God's word will fail; His promises are certain and will be fulfilled.
God’s word depends on human effort for fulfillment.
God’s word is symbolic and not literal.
questions.correctAnswer: Nothing of God's word will fail; His promises are certain and will be fulfilled.
questions.explanation: Jehu declares that nothing of the word of the LORD will fall to the ground, affirming the doctrine of divine faithfulness and sovereignty in fulfilling His promises as in 2 Kings 10:10.

questions.question: How does Jehu’s destruction of Ahab’s house and priests in 2 Kings 10:11 reveal God’s justice?
options: It shows God’s mercy toward sinners.
It demonstrates God’s judgment against persistent idolatry and sin.
It reveals God’s indifference to human wickedness.
It indicates God’s preference for political power over righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God’s judgment against persistent idolatry and sin.
questions.explanation: Jehu’s complete destruction of Ahab’s lineage and priests is evidence of God’s righteous judgment against sin and idolatry as recorded in 2 Kings 10:11.

questions.question: What does Jehu’s alliance with Jehonadab the son of Rechab in 2 Kings 10:15-16 symbolize in theological terms?
options: The unification of political factions for power.
The joining of zealots committed to the LORD’s covenant and purity.
A compromise with Baal worshippers.
A political marriage to secure peace.
questions.correctAnswer: The joining of zealots committed to the LORD’s covenant and purity.
questions.explanation: Jehu’s greeting and alliance with Jehonadab, who was known for his faithfulness to the LORD’s commands, symbolizes a theological unity of zeal for covenant purity as shown in 2 Kings 10:15-16.

questions.question: How does Jehu’s destruction of Baal worship in 2 Kings 10:18-28 illustrate the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves tolerating sinful practices for peace.
Sanctification requires the complete removal of idolatry and dedication to God alone.
Sanctification is a gradual process without decisive action.
Sanctification is irrelevant to Old Testament practices.
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification requires the complete removal of idolatry and dedication to God alone.
questions.explanation: Jehu’s deliberate and thorough destruction of Baal worship demonstrates sanctification as separation from sin and consecration to God, as narrated in 2 Kings 10:18-28.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine rewarding and human failure is conveyed by 2 Kings 10:30 and 2 Kings 10:31?
options: God rewards obedience but allows consequences for unrepented sin.
God rewards sin and punishes obedience.
Human behavior has no impact on divine reward.
God rewards only kings, regardless of their heart.
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards obedience but allows consequences for unrepented sin.
questions.explanation: Verse 30 shows God rewarding Jehu’s obedience with dynastic promises, while verse 31 reveals Jehu’s failure to fully obey, illustrating the tension between divine reward and human imperfection.

questions.question: In light of 2 Kings 10:32-33, what does the LORD’s action of ‘cutting Israel short’ reveal about His sovereignty?
options: God’s sovereignty is limited by human kings.
God exercises sovereign judgment over nations through external enemies.
God is powerless against foreign rulers.
God’s sovereignty is only over spiritual matters.
questions.correctAnswer: God exercises sovereign judgment over nations through external enemies.
questions.explanation: The LORD’s use of Hazael to smite Israel shows His sovereign control over geopolitical events as instruments of His judgment, as seen in 2 Kings 10:32-33.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Jehu’s reign concluding in 2 Kings 10:34-36 contribute to the biblical theology of kingship?
options: It shows that kingship is permanent and unchanging.
It highlights the transient nature of human kingship under divine authority.
It teaches that kings are divine beings.
It suggests kingship is irrelevant to Israel’s story.
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the transient nature of human kingship under divine authority.
questions.explanation: Jehu’s death and succession emphasize that human kingship is temporary and subject to God’s sovereign will, as recorded in 2 Kings 10:34-36.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by His fulfillment of Elijah’s prophecy through Jehu in 2 Kings 10:10 and 2 Kings 10:17?
options: God’s mercy toward the wicked.
God’s faithfulness to His word and promises.
God’s forgetfulness of past covenants.
God’s indifference to Israel’s sins.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His word and promises.
questions.explanation: God’s fulfillment of Elijah’s prophecy through Jehu’s actions demonstrates His unwavering faithfulness to His word, as seen in 2 Kings 10:10 and 10:17.

questions.question: Considering 2 Kings 10:29, what does Jehu’s failure to depart from Jeroboam’s sins teach about the doctrine of sanctification and human weakness?
options: Sanctification is always perfect in Old Testament kings.
Human leaders may be zealous yet still fall short of full obedience.
Jehu was fully sanctified and sinless.
Jehu’s sin was irrelevant to his reign.
questions.correctAnswer: Human leaders may be zealous yet still fall short of full obedience.
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that although Jehu was zealous against Baal, he failed to remove the golden calf idolatry, illustrating human weakness in sanctification.

questions.question: How does Jehu’s call for a great sacrifice to Baal in 2 Kings 10:19-21 serve as a strategic act in God's plan?
options: It was a genuine worship of Baal.
It was a deceptive tactic to gather Baal worshippers to be destroyed.
It was an act of political alliance with Baal priests.
It was meant to appease Baal.
questions.correctAnswer: It was a deceptive tactic to gather Baal worshippers to be destroyed.
questions.explanation: Jehu cleverly used the sacrifice to lure Baal worshippers together for their destruction, fulfilling God’s judgment as in 2 Kings 10:19-21.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about divine judgment and covenant promise can be drawn from Jehu’s zeal in 2 Kings 10:16 and God’s promise in 2 Kings 10:30?
options: Human zeal guarantees eternal life without divine promise.
Divine promises encourage zeal, but zeal without full obedience is incomplete.
Covenant promises are unrelated to human actions.
Zeal replaces the need for divine promise.
questions.correctAnswer: Divine promises encourage zeal, but zeal without full obedience is incomplete.
questions.explanation: Jehu’s zeal (10:16) is encouraged by God’s covenant promise (10:30), yet his incomplete obedience shows zeal alone is insufficient, highlighting the balance of divine promise and human responsibility.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's command to Jehu to kill Ahab’s descendants is immoral and unjust. What does 2 Kings 10:5-11 actually teach about divine justice and judgment?
options: God’s justice involves executing judgment on persistent sin and covenant unfaithfulness.
God arbitrarily punishes people without cause.
God is indifferent to human sin.
God approves of all human actions.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice involves executing judgment on persistent sin and covenant unfaithfulness.
questions.explanation: The passage shows divine justice in punishing Ahab’s house for persistent idolatry and rebellion, affirming God’s holiness and covenant faithfulness, as in 2 Kings 10:5-11.

questions.question: How does Jehu’s execution of Baal worshippers and destruction of Baal’s temple in 2 Kings 10:25-27 reflect God's holiness?
options: God’s holiness requires the removal of false gods and idolatry.
God’s holiness is indifferent to worship practices.
God allows all religions to coexist equally.
God’s holiness tolerates idolatry.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness requires the removal of false gods and idolatry.
questions.explanation: Jehu’s decisive action against Baal worship illustrates the necessity of purity and holiness in worship, consistent with God’s nature as holy, shown in 2 Kings 10:25-27.

questions.question: What does Jehu’s killing of Ahaziah’s brothers in 2 Kings 10:13-14 reveal about the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness in the broader redemptive narrative?
options: Covenant unfaithfulness leads to the judgment of entire families.
Covenant unfaithfulness has no consequences.
God protects all family members regardless of sin.
Judgment is only on the individual sinner.
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant unfaithfulness leads to the judgment of entire families.
questions.explanation: The killing of Ahaziah’s brothers shows that covenant disobedience affects not only individuals but also their families, reflecting God’s righteous judgment in salvation history, as in 2 Kings 10:13-14.
